shape.description: Tall brown knobbly pole with a shallow spiral groove, standing on an L-shaped brown base two cells long: one cell under the pole, one cell a pocket with a marble path through it, crossing from side to side. A flat brown cap tops the pole, with a slot for the M-64 sign. A green slider ring runs up and down the pole; it has hand grips and a cup that reaches over the pocket when down and holds a track end when up.
shape.sizeBasis: Rough estimate: one cell about 52 mm and one slot about 36 mm, scaled from Joey's hand in IMG_0954 and IMG_0956; no ruler measurement. Height from stack comparison, low confidence.

accepts: two floor cells in a line

physics.behaviour: Hand-armed magnet lift. A child pushes the green slider down until it locks at the base. A metal marble rolling into the pocket unlocks it, the magnet grips the marble, and the slider whizzes up the pole, twisting round it, and tips the marble onto the T-15 at the top. Then it stays up until a hand pushes it down again. When it is up, or for a plain marble, the marble rolls straight through the pocket and out the far side: in Level 1 into M-07. No batteries. Adds about 6.5 slots of height, once per arming.

evidence.shows: Left: two hands push the green slider down, closed lock icon. Right: open lock icon, metal marbles arrive along T-06, slider rises with curved arrows, marble leaves along yellow T-15 at top. Only metal marbles shown

evidence.source: trex_plans_07.png step 1-7 main view, inset and map
evidence.shows: Level 1: pocket at D7, pole at E7. T-06 from D5 enters W side, M-07 on E side, T-15 at top leaves W toward the D3 stack
Level 3: pocket at B7, pole at B8. T-06 from D7 enters S side, T-03 from A6 on N side, T-15 at top runs S to the F7 stack. Same handedness as Level 1
Batteries only for the T-Rex and the Elevator, so this piece has none

assumptions: A spring raises the slider and the metal marble's magnetism unlocks it: both inferred from the lock icons, the arrows and the need for hand arming; no text states them.
Plain marble passes through, inferred: M-07 sits past the pocket in Level 1 and no other route reaches it. Plan page 02 feeds from port b, the plans feed from port a; ports treated as equal.
Top port height about 7.5 from T-15 falling about 1.5 slots to the h6 block at D3 and F7.
Pocket port height 1 from T-06 and T-03 meeting height 1 blocks.
faces uses E=+x, W=-x, S=+y, N=-y, in the piece's own frame. Heights are slots above the floor when the piece stands on the floor or, where stated, above the top of its supports.
openQuestions: Does a plain marble trip the lock? Does it pass through when armed?
Does a marble wait in the pocket if the slider is up, or roll on?
What does the top cup do at the T-15: does the marble roll off or get scraped off?
